mercy_translation.text:
Suppose the whole body is activated and illuminated by a human person, and someone says it is absurd for the person's power also to be present in the toe. Such a person would be considered foolish, because while granting that the person penetrates and acts in the whole, he forbids him to be present in the part.

In the same way, someone who grants and believes that the Word of God is in the universe and that the whole is enlightened and moved by him should not think it absurd that one human body also be moved and enlightened by him.

If they think the Savior's manifestation in a human being is unfitting because the human race is created and came into being from nothing, then it is time for them to expel him from creation as well; for creation too came from non-being into being through the Word.

But if, although creation is created, it is not absurd for the Word to be in it, then neither is it absurd for him to be in a human being. Whatever they think about the whole, they must also think about the part, for, as I said before, the human being is a part of the whole.

Therefore it is not at all unfitting for the Word to be in a human being, while all things are enlightened, moved, and sustained by him and in him. Even their own writers say: “In him we live and move and are.”

What, then, is worthy of mockery in what we say if the Word has used as an instrument for manifestation something in which he already is? If he were not in it, he could not have used it. But if we have already established that he is in the whole and in its parts, what is unbelievable about his also manifesting himself in those things in which he is?

By his own powers he is wholly present in each thing and in all things, ordering everything without envy. If he had wished, he could have used the sun, moon, heaven, earth, water, or fire as a voice by which to make himself and his Father known, since he holds all things together, is with all and in each part, and invisibly shows himself through them. In the same way, it would not be absurd that, while ordering all things and giving life to the universe, he wished to make himself known through human beings and therefore used a human body as an instrument for the manifestation of truth and knowledge of the Father. Humanity too is a part of the whole.

And just as the mind, being throughout the whole human being, is signified through one part of the body—the tongue—and no one says that the essence of the mind is diminished because of this, so the Word, being throughout all things, does nothing unfitting if he uses a human instrument. For, as I said before, if it were unfitting for him to use a body as an instrument, it would also be unfitting for him to be in the whole universe.

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The body/toe and mind/tongue analogies argue that manifestation through a part does not imply confinement or diminution of the Word.
'Instrument' language here concerns the body as the medium of divine manifestation and should be read together with Athanasius' insistence on the reality of Christ's humanity.
